name: GitHub Copilot SDK — direct to APIM
summary: Copilot SDK BYOK provider pointed straight at the APIM AI Gateway, bypassing Foundry entirely.
description: APIM already exposes an OpenAI-compatible surface, so `base_url = "https://<apim>.azure-api.net/openai/v1/"` + APIM subscription key (or a static JWT via `bearerToken`) lets the Copilot SDK talk to your AI Gateway without any Foundry involvement. In this topology there is no `{conn}/{model}` BYOM prefix — the model string is just the APIM deployment name, because you're already at the gateway.
notes:
Verified 2026-07-29 via the `copilot-canary` hosted agent (deployed by the `ai-gateway-pe-testing` infra repo — runs inside the Foundry VNet with line-of-sight to APIM's private endpoint). Two invocation paths are supported (in preference order): (1) if `HOSTED_AGENT_NAME_COPILOT_CANARY` is wired, the test invokes the canary; (2) otherwise, a direct `CopilotClient` call from the runner — only works when the runner has line-of-sight to APIM. GitHub-hosted runners hit `403 public network access ... is disabled` on path (2), which is why we ship the canary.

Canary exercises the **full-fidelity** path: `wire_api: "responses"` against a **GPT-5.1 deployment**, so the Copilot CLI's built-in `apply_patch` tool (declared as an OpenAI custom-grammar tool — GPT-5-only Responses API feature) is present in the tool schema and the test genuinely validates BYOK works for GPT-5-class models. `wire_api: "completions"` also works but silently drops `apply_patch`, so it's a lower-fidelity signal.

**Key BYOK wiring gotchas (all verified locally against `agent-framework-github-copilot 1.0.0`):**

- `provider` alone is not enough — must also pass `model=<wire_model>` in `default_options`, or the CLI falls back to the empty CAPI model list and errors with `Session error: No model available`.
- APIM's OpenAI-compatible base is `/inference/openai/v1/`, not `/openai/v1/`.
- `instructions=` is a top-level `GitHubCopilotAgent` constructor arg, NOT a `default_options` key (would raise `TypeError: create_session() got an unexpected keyword argument 'instructions'`).
- Reasoning models (GPT-5.1) are noticeably slower per turn than gpt-4o — bump `timeout` in `default_options` to 180s or the SDK's 60s session.idle limit trips on multi-tool-call probes (e.g. write-then-read).
- Auth on the direct path uses `Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key` or `bearer_token`; the canary uses the hosted agent's managed identity scoped to `https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/.default`.

Verbatim green response from canary invocation (2026-07-29, code_version `2026-07-29-gpt5-responses-timeout180`):

> `{"name": "chat", "ok": true, "output_text": "12", "latency_ms": 23622}`

See `test.py`. For the built-in-tools companion card (shell + files exercised through the same route), see `copilot-sdk-builtin-tools`. Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities.
